boundary_verdict: A Detroit city-proper municipal boundary is VIABLE BUT DECAPITATING — usable as a base geometry, fatal if used alone. 16 of 20 oracle entries (80%) fall inside the City of Detroit boundary; 4 fall outside, and they are disproportionately top-tier. The #1 draw by every independent measure — The Henry Ford campus (Henry Ford Museum of American Innovation + Greenfield Village + Ford Rouge Factory Tour, ~1.8M visitors/yr, Michigan's most-visited attraction, named by Michigan.org, Frommer's, Fodor's Choice, Time Out #6, U.S. News, Lonely Planet) — is in DEARBORN, ~15.5 km west of downtown. The Detroit Zoo, despite the name and despite being owned by the City of Detroit, is in ROYAL OAK/Huntington Woods (Oakland County), ~18 km out and ~3 km north of the 8 Mile boundary. Cranbrook is in BLOOMFIELD HILLS, ~32 km out. So a city-proper query silently drops the single entry a visitor would most regret missing, plus two more that appear on the state tourism board's own four-item shortlist. Belle Isle is the counter-case that a naive "state park = not city" heuristic gets wrong: it is a Michigan DNR-operated state park but lies wholly INSIDE the Detroit municipal boundary (Wayne County), ~5.5 km from downtown, and must be retained. A radius fix is poor: 16 km captures Dearborn but not the Zoo; 18 km captures the Zoo but not Cranbrook; 35 km captures Cranbrook but sweeps in most of Oakland and Macomb County suburbia (Somerset Collection, Birmingham, Troy) that no guidebook ranks. The correct boundary is the DMO's own footprint — City of Detroit plus explicit named-municipality inclusion of Dearborn, Royal Oak/Huntington Woods, Bloomfield Hills (and, for a longer list, Grosse Pointe Shores for the Edsel & Eleanor Ford House). Visit Detroit itself markets the tri-county Wayne/Oakland/Macomb region, not the city polygon. Verdict: scoring a pipeline on Detroit city-proper alone caps achievable recall at ~80% and guarantees the miss of rank #1 and #4.
category_profile:
Detroit's recall problem is a TAGGING problem more than a geometry problem, and the failure mode is specific: the city's biggest draws are industrial heritage, Motown, skyscraper architecture, and public art — none of which a European-derived whitelist (castle/cathedral/palace/museum/viewpoint) reliably reaches. Verified against live Overpass data:

TAGGED AND SAFE (7/20, all tourism=museum-family): DIA, Motown Museum, Charles H. Wright, Ford Piquette, Henry Ford Museum, Greenfield Village, Detroit Zoo (tourism=zoo), plus Guardian Building and Heidelberg Project on tourism=attraction. A museum+zoo+attraction whitelist gets these nine.

OUTRIGHT UNTAGGED — carry a Wikidata QID but NO primary attraction tag (6/20, ~30% of the oracle): Michigan Central Station (building=train_station only), Renaissance Center (building=commercial only), Fisher Building (building=office only), Ambassador Bridge (bridge=yes on the carriageway ways only), Eastern Market (place=neighbourhood + landuse=commercial, no marketplace tag), Detroit RiverWalk (fifteen highway=path/cycleway ways, no named entity, no route relation). These are unreachable by any tourism/historic/leisure predicate and only recoverable via a wikidata-presence or building-name heuristic.

TAGGED BUT OFF-WHITELIST (5/20): Spirit of Detroit and Monument to Joe Louis are tourism=artwork — correct OSM practice, but artwork is the tag most commonly dropped from attraction whitelists, and Detroit's mural/public-art culture (Murals in the Market, Grand River Creative Corridor, The Belt, Dequindre Cut's 35+ pieces, Dabls MBAD Bead Museum) lives almost entirely under tourism=artwork or nothing at all. Fox Theatre is amenity=theatre with no tourism or historic tag. Comerica Park/Ford Field/Little Caesars Arena are leisure=stadium. Belle Isle — the #1 in-city green space — is leisure=nature_reserve + place=island, not leisure=park and not tourism=*, so both a park query and an attraction query miss the island itself while catching only its Conservatory and Aquarium.

Practical implication: a pipeline restricted to tourism=museum|attraction|zoo|aquarium|viewpoint scores roughly 9-11/20 on Detroit. Adding tourism=artwork, amenity=theatre, leisure=stadium, leisure=nature_reserve and a Wikidata-QID-on-building fallback is what moves it past 15 — and only widening the municipal boundary past the city line moves it past 16.
